name: University of Michigan — Kresge Hearing Research Institute
focus: Susan Shore's lab developed targeted bimodal auditory-somatosensory stimulation; in her double-blinded crossover trial more than 60% of participants had meaningful symptom reduction after 6 weeks of active treatment. Shore co-founded Auricle Inc. to commercialize the device.

name: Trinity College Dublin / Neuromod Devices
focus: Brendan Conlon (TCD/Neuromod) and CSO Hubert Lim ran the TENT-A1/A2/A3 bimodal sound + tongue stimulation trials behind Lenire, the first device FDA De Novo authorized for tinnitus (March 2023). TCD began recruiting the NITESGON-ADT bimodal trial in January 2026.

name: University of Regensburg / Tinnitus Research Initiative
focus: Berthold Langguth's group is a hub of the Tinnitus Research Initiative and coordinated the EU UNITI-RCT (N=461, five countries; Nature Communications 2025) — the largest trial comparing single versus combined tinnitus treatments.

name: University of Auckland — Hearing & Tinnitus Research
focus: Grant Searchfield's group developed the 'digital polytherapeutic' personalized sound-therapy approach (RCT 2022). In August 2026 the university spun the 30-year research program into startup TrueSilence Therapeutics, delivering clinician-guided 90-day programs via smartphone.

name: Karolinska Institutet
focus: Christopher Cederroth's Translational Auditory Neuroscience group leads tinnitus genetics and epidemiology, including the TIGER consortium and a 2025 GWAS meta-analysis implicating amygdala and midbrain circuits, plus work on sex differences in tinnitus.

name: UMC Utrecht
focus: The Stokroos group researches tinnitus subtyping and cochlear implantation for tinnitus — in a 72-patient prospective study, 60% of implanted tinnitus patients had clinically significant reduction at 3 months — alongside neuromodulation, CBT and mindfulness work.

name: NIHR Nottingham Biomedical Research Centre
focus: Derek Hoare leads the hearing theme covering tinnitus and hyperacusis; current work includes closing the gap between CBT evidence and NHS audiologist-delivered care, cochlear-implant tinnitus research, and wearable-device evaluation (WHITBY tDCS trial).

name: University of Oxford
focus: The Institute of Biomedical Engineering (Robin Cleveland) runs a Tinnitus Quest-funded transcranial ultrasound stimulation project targeting deep-brain tinnitus circuits; Oxford neuroscientists also lead research linking non-REM slow-wave sleep to tinnitus suppression.

name: NIDCD (National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders)
focus: The lead US federal funder of hearing and tinnitus research (estimating more than 25 million US adults with tinnitus). Funds tinnitus R01 grants, SBIR programs, fellowships and clinical research centers — including the NIH funding behind the Shore bimodal trial.

name: Sound Pharmaceuticals
focus: Developer of SPI-1005 (oral ebselen). Its STOPMD-3 Phase 3 in Meniere's disease met co-primary endpoints (company-reported, Dec 2024) with patient-reported tinnitus improvement in the open-label extension, and received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation in December 2025.
